papers.title_en: Toward Agentic Robotics: A Large-Scale Study of Harness Design for Robot-Use Agents
papers.authors: Yuxiang Lai, Jike Zhong, Yu-Jhe Li, Lan Wang, Chengzhi Liu, Youbao Tang, Ming Li, Xi Xiao, Xiaofeng Yang, Liang Zhao, Zheda Mai, Ruixi Fan
papers.evidence: VLM推理感知结合VLA控制，通过策略框架编排
papers.tldr: VLM可作机器人智能体，却难以精确预测3D夹爪位姿；VLA/WAM控制快而稳，但在域偏移和长程推理中易失效。本文用策略harness连接VLM推理与VLA/WAM控制，覆盖8个仿真基准、6个VLM和15个检查点，完成47万次rollout。七组实验表明，harness需同时适配两类模型能力，明确策略代码结构、工具介入位置与调用VLM的时机。参考方案X-Harness无需更新权重即可组合这些发现，在记忆、推理和域偏移上最高提升42.8分。
papers.abstract_en: Recent vision-language models (VLMs) can act as robot-use agents that understand diverse scenes and control robots through policy code and tools. However, they predict 3D gripper poses poorly even with extended reasoning, struggling with precise manipulation. Vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action (WAM) models are the opposite: they execute fast, smooth control on trained tasks, yet fail under domain shifts or when tasks require long-horizon memory and reasoning. Agentic robots therefore combine VLM reasoning and perception with precise VLA/WAM control through a policy harness. Yet harness design spans thousands of configurations, shifting success by tens of points with the same models. Moreover, testing even one design takes thousands of rollouts at high API and GPU cost, so prior works often commit to a single design chosen from few alternatives. To guide harness design, we evaluate over 470,000 rollouts across eight simulation benchmarks, six VLMs, and 15 VLA/WAM checkpoints. Seven controlled studies show effective harnesses must adapt to both VLM and VLA/WAM capabilities. Our findings specify what structure the VLM's policy code needs, where VLA manipulation needs help from tools and policy code, and when to involve the VLM at test time. The reference recipe X-Harness shows that these findings compose without weight updates, lifting base policies up to $+42.8$ points across memory, reasoning, and domain shifts.

papers.title_en: SayDo: Benchmarking the Safety of Frontier Models from Chat to Closed-Loop Robot Control
papers.evidence: 前沿视觉语言模型作为高层机器人控制器，沿具身梯度进行安全评测
papers.tldr: 前沿视觉语言模型正被用作机器人高层控制器，但其安全性几乎只在文本对话中评估。SayDo 基准用11个实验室与家庭任务，将良性指令与场景隐患配对，并沿具身梯度在6种设置中测试，从聊天问答延伸到模拟机械臂闭环控制。对6个开放/闭权VLM共11,480回合的评测显示，危险动作率从聊天14%升至模拟器47%，最受影响模型从2%升至80%，且升幅主要来自开放权重模型。这表明文本安全评测不能预测同一模型作为机器人控制器时的安全行为。
papers.abstract_en: Frontier vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as high-level robot controllers, yet their safety is evaluated almost entirely in text. We introduce SayDo, a benchmark that assesses the propensity of frontier models to cause harm in embodied contexts. SayDo comprises eleven laboratory and household tasks that pair a benign instruction with a hazard latent in the scene. Tasks are implemented in six settings along an embodiment gradient, from chat questions about an imagined robot to closed-loop control of a simulated robot arm. Benign controls, safe-alternative variants and scripted operator pushback complement each task. Across six open- and closed-weight VLMs and 11,480 episodes, hazardous-action rates rise from 14% in chat to 47% in the simulator, and from 2% to 80% for the most affected model. The increase is largely driven by open-weight models. We find that models flag hazards before acting in 73% of unsafe episodes and give way to pushback about twice as often when controlling robots as in chat. The safest models also show signs of overcaution on benign controls. Safety evaluations run in text therefore do not predict the safety behavior of the same models when used as robot controllers.

papers.title_en: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
papers.authors: Yiyang Du, Yuxuan Kuang, Qitao Zhao, Yixuan Wang, Zhanqiu Guo, Yi Xu, Xin Li, Wenbin He, Liu Ren, Chenyan Xiong
papers.evidence: 前沿多模态语言智能体直接控制机器人并进行动作级评估
papers.tldr: 前沿多模态智能体已能通过底层数值动作直接控制机器人，但现有基准只报告回合级成功率，无法说明它们成功与失败的具体机制。本文提出AgentRoboCritic意图锚定批评框架：策略智能体为每个动作声明局部意图，批评器再对照该意图评估动作结果与失败模式。在12个操作基准上的动作级分析揭示了闭环纠错、语义grounding与零样本操作能力，也定位了抓取、对齐等物理瓶颈。作者还发布1.28万条标注动作与微调开源批评器Muse-Glimmer-30B，失败模式准确率由32.58%升至74.24%。
papers.abstract_en: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.

papers.authors: Xiao-Ming Wu, Kang Liao, Yuexiao Ma, Taolin Zhang, Mingqian Zhou, Nuo Chen, Ziming Li, Yihang Luo, Rui Li, Zhonghua Wu, Tianyu Xie, Xiawu Zheng, Zhongang Cai, Zhi Hou, Chen Change Loy
papers.evidence: 研究机器人智能体循环中的规划与动作执行
papers.tldr: 前沿多模态模型可直接作为机器人闭环策略，但其harness设计原则尚不清晰。Embo-Harness系统研究提示、规划、动作执行与工具使用四个环节，并将六条实证发现凝练为实用配方。该配方优先利用模型原生视觉推理与工具使用能力，而非手工规划、技能或动作先验。在RoboLab-120上取得83.3%成功率，较最强基线高26.2个百分点，并在四项真实操作任务20次零样本试验中成功15次。
papers.abstract_en: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe. This recipe prioritizes interfaces that exploit the model's native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors, and identifies effective choices for action representation, chunking, reasoning effort, visual observations, short multi-action sequences, and policy refinement. On RoboLab-120, Embo-Harness achieves an 83.3\% success rate, outperforming the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points. It also succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot trials across four real-world manipulation tasks. Beyond performance, controlled interventions indicate that the studied model depends more strongly on accurate spatial target estimation than on explicit low-level joint or trajectory generation. These results provide both a practical recipe for building strong frontier-model-as-policy harnesses and a clearer account of the capabilities that drive their performance.
